chapter_note: The oldest layer here is largely a numbered, systematic correspondential teaching: (a) seven benefits of the Sun vs. seven evils of Night, (b) five archetypes in the Sun, and (c) three further Sun-qualities corresponding to the Father of Greatness. Later hands add (i) a hagiographic dialogue setting (“the apostle… among his disciples”), (ii) polemic/application against “sects,” (iii) a scriptural/legal anti-Jewish passage about a “law” forbidding worship of the sun, and (iv) explicit Gospel/NT overlay at the close (Thomas saying; “children of light/day” language) plus concluding blessings/exhortation (editorial fatigue in the second half).

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic hagiographic scene-setting (“Once again, the apostle… among the congregation of his disciples”).
Depends on external ‘law’/scriptural polemic (OT citation flagged in apparatus); cosmos→contemporary/scriptural-juridical argument rather than impersonal system exposition.
Present-tense application and polemic (“even today”), rhetorical blame of “people” for blindness—application voice rather than structural cosmology.
Rhetorical exhortation (“Shall they not see them?”) introducing a list; functions as homiletic bridge.

paragraphs.core_text: The first good thing that it does for them is its light, which it shines upon them. It opens the eyes of all mankind. They see underfoot as they walk by it. It takes away the blindness of the night, which made them blind with its darkness.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Numbered correspondential schema (first of seven), impersonal mechanics of Light vs. night/darkness within the created order.

paragraphs.core_text: The second: When (the sun) is come to the world, with its coming it shall bring calm and peace to the entire world. With its coming it shall also take away from them all the fear and trembling, which their heart is filled with the whole night; for it shall take away the darkness present by its light, and sweep it out. Also, this is how it extinguishes fear by its calm.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Second item in a structured heptad; describes a process-mechanism (Light dispels Darkness/fear).

paragraphs.core_text: The third is its vigil; because when (the sun) comes to the world all sleeping mankind shall arise and awake. And the watchmen too shall cease from watching. The guards who sit at the gates of camps, they break vigil at the watchposts, because of its light that has shone upon them in the world.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Third item of the heptad; still expository and iterative, continuing the numbered system.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.160⟩ The fourth: It shall nourish, and give strength, taste and scent, to the trees and fruits and vegetables, and all the herbs, and the flowers and grasses, which are upon the entire earth.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Correspondential register (strength/taste/scent) typical of older mapping style; impersonal description.

paragraphs.core_text: The fifth: When (the sun) shines in all the world, the evil reptile and the sharp-toothed beasts that are filled of wickedness, they shall flee to hiding in their dens.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fifth item; Light’s dominance over hostile life-forms presented as a regular cosmic effect.

paragraphs.core_text: The sixth: When it shines its light, the wound of any person is eased from pain. Its light shall melt away the evil arts of every doer of wickedness.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Sixth item; Light as a dissolver of ‘evil arts’ (magical/demonic efficacy) is expressed as cosmological causation.

paragraphs.core_text: The seventh: (The sun) shall display and manifest to the world the sign of the splendour of the aeons of light, from which it has come out; it here in this world being their sign. It brings light to the whole of creation.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Seventh item closes the heptad with explicit sign/correspondence logic: Sun as ‘sign’ of the aeons of Light.
Application polemic against ‘sects of error’ and evaluative rhetoric; not impersonal system description.

paragraphs.core_text: the night, for it has all wickednesses therein. Every occasion, would the night fall, it shall do seven evils in the world.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed audience-address / discourse management: “Now, just as I have shown you the sun… hear also what I teach you…”. This is an editorial teaching-to-audience pivot rather than the heptadic schematic content itself.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core heptad-setup preserved (night does seven evils), but the paragraph begins with direct address and authorial prompting typical of later application voice.

paragraphs.core_text: The first wickedness that the night shall do in the world is the darkness, with which it shall fill the entire world; because when the sun sinks from the world and draws to it its rays, at that instant the shadow of the night shall spread out over the whole world. The eyes of the people fill with blackness. They neither see nor wonder with their eyes, because of the darkness of the night which shall fill the whole world.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Numbered counter-heptad mirrors the earlier structure; mechanistic account of the spread of darkness.

paragraphs.core_text: The second evil thing that the night shall do is its fear; because when its shadow looms forth, its fear and its trembling shall possess all of mankind. The entire world shall fill of the night.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Second item of the seven-evils schema; continues the impersonal iterative pattern.

paragraphs.core_text: The third: When the night falls, all creatures take up revolt. They rebel in their heart, to do wickedness and perdition.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Third item; Darkness-as-influx effect expressed as a general cosmic tendency.

paragraphs.core_text: The fourth: The heaviness of sleep shall lay upon them, and they fall asleep; they slumber and doze, and they are like these corpses in the night.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fourth item; correspondential effect of night (sleep/corpse-likeness) stated as lawlike.

paragraphs.core_text: The fifth is its ugliness; again, when the night would fall, the form of the people shall be hidden in the darkness and the ugliness of the night. The beauty and the form of men and women shall not be displayed before one another, because of its darkness and its ugliness, which it shall spread out over all their forms.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fifth item; sensory/esthetic register (‘beauty/form/ugliness’) fits the older correspondential style.

paragraphs.core_text: The evil beasts shall come out, and all the reptiles that are filled with wickedness, from their dens. And they stalk in the night. Also, the demons and fiends find power to do wickedness in the night. Again, the blows and buffets and wounds and discharges shall torment people in the night; because in it the whole of evil shall find strength.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed explicit moral-social catalogue applied to human society: “At that instant evil people shall come out to do wickedness; the adulterers, and the robbers and poisoners.” This shifts from cosmic/night mechanics to contemporary vice-listing.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core-like night/Darkness mechanics (beasts, demons, ‘evil finds strength’) are present, but the opening vice list is an application graft.

paragraphs.core_text: The seventh: The night shall display the sign of the darkness, its father. It has arisen out of its essence; because this night that came out of this first Darkness has been displayed in the world. Note this night, the shadow of this first Darkness, the one that is entwined and bound in all things above and below.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Closes the counter-heptad with explicit sign/correspondence logic; Darkness is personified as ‘father’ with ‘essence’.
Summative ‘I have taught you’ plus polemic against sects; functions as homiletic application rather than the schematic itself.

paragraphs.core_text: There are five archetypes occur in the sun, it making them [...] as it finds the world.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue/frame attribution: “Once again he ramified. He says to his disciples:”.
paragraphs.temporal_note: A new numbered structure (five archetypes) begins, but is introduced by a redactional dialogue marker that must be stripped from the core.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.162⟩ The first is its light; for it illumines by its light the world, and all the creatures who exist in it.
paragraphs.temporal_note: First of five archetypes; concise, impersonal mapping.

paragraphs.core_text: The second is its beauty; because when it shines, it shall flood beauty and loveliness upon all creatures and everything.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Second archetype; sensory/esthetic correspondential register.

paragraphs.core_text: The third is its peace; for, again, when the sun would shine on the world, all people shall receive affection through it, and give peace to one another.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Third archetype; continues list-structure; still framed as an effect-law of the Sun.

paragraphs.core_text: The fourth is the life of the living soul, which it shall release from all the bonds and fetters of heaven and earth.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fourth archetype; explicitly Manichaean cosmological mechanic (release of the living soul from bonds).

paragraphs.core_text: The fifth: It gives a strength to the elements; and also it gives a scent and a taste to the entire Cross of the Light.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fifth archetype; classic correspondential registers (elements; scent/taste) and a named cosmic structure (Cross of the Light).

paragraphs.core_text: its light illumines more than all lights that occur in the world. Also, its beauty is more beautiful than all the beauties of mankind. Again, its peace is more surpassing than all the powers and guards who exist in the world. Its releasing action, by which it releases the living soul, is a full day ahead of all releasing actions! The strength that it gives to its limbs is a great strength, being mightier than all strengths!
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed direct audience-address preface: “So, you yourselves see that…”.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Primarily an intensifying recapitulation of the five archetypes (still cosmological), but introduced with a second-person exhortative cue.

paragraphs.core_text: Once again, there are another three archetypes made apparent by the sun, in respect of the mystery of the first greatness.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Introduces a new triad with a clear correspondential target (‘mystery of the first greatness’); impersonal and structural.

paragraphs.core_text: The first is the filling up of the disk of its ship; because its ship has filled up every season, and shall not wane at all, the way that the ship of the moon wanes. This continuous filling, by which it is filled, displays the mystery of the Father, the great greatness; from whom all the powers and the gods have come forth. He shall never wane, nor shall lack ever exist in him!
paragraphs.temporal_note: Explicit correspondence: Sun-ship fullness ↔ Father’s inexhaustibility; systematic comparison with moon-ship waning.

paragraphs.core_text: The second: (The sun's) light surpasses the light of all the stars, and all the lights that occur in the universe; corresponding to the mystery of the light of the Father; for his light surpasses and is greater than the light of his aeons.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Second correspondence: Sun’s light superiority ↔ Father’s light surpassing aeons; formal ‘corresponding to’ marker in a cosmological frame.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.163⟩ The third: This sun is very high above all else. It surpasses the height of all the mountains and hills that exist upon the entire earth, corresponding to the mystery of the Father of Greatness; for he is high above all the household of his light-earth. Also, because the Father himself is high above all the heights and the mountains of his light-earth. He is 'filled up' in his image [all] the time and every hour from eternity to eternity!
paragraphs.temporal_note: Third correspondence: height of Sun ↔ transcendence of the Father of Greatness; strongly cosmological (‘light-earth’, eternity-to-eternity).

paragraphs.core_text: The mystery of the night and that of the day, which daily come forth in the world. Now, the mystery of the light and the mystery of the darkness are displayed daily in the created order.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed exhortative/polemic wrapper: “[Beho]ld the two mysteries I have taught you, O my beloved ones!” and “The sects have not seen them in their error!”.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Contains a succinct core thesis (daily manifestation of the two mysteries), but framed with affectionate address and anti-sect polemic.

paragraphs.core_text: The mystery of the first great light is the sun, which is this second light-giver, the one that comes daily to the world. It displays all the marks of its graces, displaying and signifying on its own behalf that it is good, out of the essence of the good. It came from the good Father and appeared in this world.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmological identification of Sun as ‘second light-giver’ and as sign of the Good/Father; system-internal metaphysics of origin/essence.

paragraphs.core_text: In contrast, this night that is made of fear exists after the mystery of the darkness. Behold too the mystery of its essence! It displays it in the world in all these wickednesses. It displays this mystery daily in the world, but the sects know it not in their error. They do not distinguish the mystery of the light from that of the darkness.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core contrastive cosmology (Night after the mystery of Darkness), though it includes a polemical tag about ‘sects’ that may reflect redactional pressure.
Explicit saviour-saying (Thomas) introduced as authoritative allusion; entered via Gospel tradition rather than the impersonal substrate.
Dialogue attribution plus ‘children of day/light’ idiom strongly keyed to NT language (cf. 1 Thess 5); best explained as Christian overlay.
Concluding beatitude/exhortation with direct address (‘my beloved ones’) and soteriological payoff (‘inherit life eternal’)—late homiletic closure consistent with editorial fatigue.
